decisions.rationale: Basculegion uses Last Respects on Sneasler (since Last Respects has 150 base power after Pelipper fainted, and Sneasler takes massive damage or faints). Swampert-Mega uses Waterfall on Sneasler to secure a KO, or we can look at damage: Sneasler is weak to Ground, but Altaria is immune to Earthquake and Sneasler is a major threat with Close Combat/Dire Claw. Wait, Swampert-Mega's Waterfall into Sneasler (choice 2) hits Sneasler hard in rain. Let's check Last Respects into Sneasler (choice 1) and Waterfall into Sneasler (choice 2). Sneasler is weak to nothing from Waterfall, but it's hit neutrally. Wait, Sneasler is Fighting/Poison (weak to Psychic, Flying, Ground). Swampert's Earthquake hits Sneasler super-effectively (2x), but Earthquake hits adjacent ally Basculegion too. Swampert's Waterfall into Sneasler is neutral. However, Basculegion's Last Respects on Sneasler (choice 1) does massive damage. Let's make sure Basculegion targets Sneasler with Last Respects (1) and Swampert targets Sneasler with Waterfall (2) or Protect (7). Wait, Sneasler might use Quick Guard or Protect. But Swampert's Waterfall is contact. Let's check Sneasler's moves: Fake Out, Close Combat, Quick Guard, Dire Claw. If Sneasler uses Quick Guard, it blocks priority (Aqua Jet), but Last Respects and Waterfall are standard priority 0 moves, not blocked by Quick Guard. Thus Basculegion's Last Respects and Swampert's Waterfall will hit Sneasler through Quick Guard. Therefore, Basculegion Last Respects -> foe 2 (Sneasler) [index 1] and Swampert-Mega Waterfall -> foe 2 (Sneasler) [index 2].

reflections.summary: We lost the series 0-2 because our rain offense cores were systematically neutralized by the opponent's defensive positioning (Cloud Nine Altaria, Sturdy Archaludon, and Protect cycling) and specialized coverage like Freeze-Dry Mamoswine. Pelipper and Mega Swampert fell too early to pressure, and choice-locked Basculegion was walled by smart Protect timing and Archaludon's typing.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent's defensive utility and Sturdy/Protect pivoting, we should bring Primarina or Feraligatr for better alternative offensive angles instead of doubling down on straightforward weather setups that get exploited by Cloud Nine and defensive Dragon types.
reflections.notebook: Opponent utilizes Cloud Nine Altaria to shut down rain, Sturdy Archaludon with Thunderbolt/Flash Cannon for anti-water/fairy pressure, and frequent Protect/Helping Hand plays to stall out momentum. Standard rain speed control is unreliable against their disruption; favor versatile mixed attackers and defensive pivoting over linear Swift Swim sweepers.

reflections.summary: Won game 2 and the series 2-0 through a strong matchup plan and clean piloting. Altaria's Cloud Nine removed Pelipper's rain advantage, Mamoswine's Freeze-Dry immediately threatened the Water core, and Archaludon efficiently finished Basculegion and Whimsicott with super-effective attacks. Protect cycling preserved Altaria long enough to deny Basculegion's Choice-locked Last Respects while poison and Moonblast wore down Mega Swampert. The brought four—Altaria, Mamoswine, Sneasler, and Archaludon—were well suited to the preview; Sneasler's Fake Out created useful tempo even though it was traded for Basculegion's attack. No Mega evolution was used, and that was appropriate: retaining Cloud Nine and the Focus Sash/utility set mattered more than introducing an unsupported Mega option. There were no decision errors, and no supplied evidence identifies a specific between-game adjustment, so its effect cannot be credited or blamed; the demonstrated plan itself worked. The registered six fit reasonably well, with coherent anti-rain, anti-Water, speed-control, disruption, and coverage tools. The remaining roster did not show a materially better alternative than the selected four.
reflections.adjustment: Against a future rematch, keep the same core plan and likely the same four, but make Whimsicott a higher-priority target before it can repeatedly use Prankster Tailwind, Encore, or Moonblast. Preserve Altaria when possible, while avoiding overcommitting it to repeated Protect cycles if Whimsicott remains free to pressure it. Maintain dedicated answers to Mega Swampert and Basculegion: Cloud Nine plus Freeze-Dry remains excellent, and Archaludon's Electric and Steel coverage is valuable. No Mega holder needs to be added based on this evidence; do not replace Altaria's Cloud Nine role merely to Mega Evolve.
reflections.notebook: Opponent uses a rain-oriented Water core with Pelipper's Drizzle, Damp Rock, Protect, and possible Tailwind; Mega Swampert is a physical attacker with Earthquake, Waterfall, and Ice Punch. Cloud Nine is highly valuable because it removes the rain advantage without requiring weather control. Basculegion revealed Choice Scarf, Adaptability, and Last Respects, with Wave Crash, Aqua Jet, and Flip Turn also available; once Last Respects is selected, it can be exploited as a locked target. Whimsicott revealed Prankster, Focus Sash, Tailwind, Encore, Moonblast, and Protect, making it the key fast-support disruption threat and a priority target. Preserve Altaria when practical, but account for Whimsicott's super-effective Moonblast and Encore when planning Protect sequences. Freeze-Dry pressure and Archaludon's Electric/Steel coverage matched the opponent well; Fake Out offered useful tempo even when Sneasler was expendable. Future preparation should retain anti-rain and anti-Water coverage, a way to pressure Focus Sash support, and protection against speed-control disruption. The unused roster offered no evidenced upgrade over the selected four for this matchup.
